We need to produce a JSON object with fields:

- failure_mode
- evidence (list)
- assumptions (list)

We must follow the instructions: first do a step back: list assumptions, approach families, then propose candidates, choose one, give direction.

We must base analysis on the provided data: multiple runs with this code (turn 11 code) which includes _danger_close detection and uses _evade for any mover within 2m regardless of direction. The code also has gap logic, stop/detour, etc. The summary: out of 10 runs (9 executed), 7 pass, 2 fail. The failures: one collision at t=6.35 with mover_00; one time_limit (run with time_limit 33.5, sim_time 34.5, final distance 12.9m). So failures: 1 collision, 1 time limit (stall? progress abort?). The collision happened early (6.35 s). first_not_on_map at 1.35 s within 2m: distance 1.54 m bearing -51°, i.e., detection at 1.35 s. The code's _danger_close triggers if mover within 2m; they set _DANGER_DIST = 2.0 and _danger_close returns True if any mover within 2m (distance measured from mover center). In this collision run, first_not_on_map within 2m at t=1.35 s, but the robot didn't stop; it collided at t=6.35 s. So the detection existed but the code didn't successfully evade. Why? Possibly because after detection, the code calls _evade(pose, movers, target, False) which returns a candidate command based on scoring. But maybe the evasion fails because the target is ahead and the scoring picks a command that still leads to collision. Or maybe _danger_close detection is not effective due to early detection of mover but the evasion algorithm chooses a forward movement (maybe because of scoring). Or maybe the detection is only for movers within 2m but the mover is approaching from behind/side; the code's _evade may not handle well.

Also, the time_limit failure: run 1756116562, time_limit 33.5, sim_time 34.5, goal not reached, final distance 12.9m. The first_not_on_map within 2m is null, but within 5m at t=28.52 (dist 3.5m). So the robot didn't see any moving object within 2m, but likely got stuck or took too long. It had many stop/turn episodes (5). The robot may have been overly cautious (stop/detour) causing delays, leading to time limit.

Goal: Achieve pass for all runs within total time budget 600 sec (average <= 60 sec per run). Currently pass runs have sim times from 65 to 107 seconds, average around maybe 80 sec. Need to reduce time per run.

Thus main failure modes: collision (1) due to insufficient evasion for side/back movers; time limit (1) due to excessive stop/detour or slow speed.

We need to propose a new direction that addresses both.

First, step back: assumptions that the current design makes:

Assumption list: (maybe 5-6). For each, hold true or not.

Assumptions:

1. Moving objects will be detected within 2m before they become a collision risk. Evidence: first_not_on_map within 2m appears early in many runs (e.g., at t~59-73 s). However, in collision run detection at 1.35 s but still collides later. So assumption partially holds but detection may be late relative to speed.

2. The robot's body can be approximated by its front bumper (x=+0.34) for collision checks. Review comment says they used pose origin, causing misestimation. So assumption is false.

3. The danger detection based on distance alone (within 2m) is sufficient to trigger evasion regardless of direction. Evidence: fails for side/back mover causing collision. So assumption false.

4. The evasion planner _evade will always find a safe candidate that avoids collision if any exists. Evidence: collision shows it didn't.

5. Stop/detour thresholds (gap < _STOP_D = 1.5m) are adequate to stop before collision. Evidence: collision run had gap detection maybe not triggered because mover was behind; _front_gap only looks at front.

6. The time budget per run is not a constraint; code can be slower. Actually, total budget matters, so need faster.

Now, approach families: group previous attempts.

From attempt records:

- Turn 0: no control (fail)
- Turn 1: simple front gap stop/detour with state machine, stop_wait 5s, _STOP_D=1.0. 9/10 passes, avg 63s, one time_limit fail. (Family: simple gap-based stop/detour)
- Turn 2: candidate-based local planner, no stop/detour, all stall (0/3). (Family: candidate planner only)
- Turn 3: same as turn 1 but stop_wait reduced to 2.0s, same stop/detour logic. 9/10 passes, avg 62s, 1 collision. (Family: same as turn1 but stop_wait 2s)
- Turn 4: added danger_zone_check and speed scaling. 6/8 passes, avg 77s, 2 fails (collision, time limit). (Family: danger zone scaling)
- Turn 5: increased _SAFE_GO to 0.6, same other constants. 9/10 passes, avg 63s, 1 collision. (Family: safe_go increase)
- Turn 6: added VO safety check. 7/8 passes, avg 79s, 1 time limit. (Family: VO safety)
- Turn 7: increased TTC window to 2.0s. 8/10 passes, avg 62s, 2 collisions. (Family: larger TTC)
- Turn 8: increased _STOP_D to 1.5 (more conservative). 9/9 passes, avg 65s, no fails. (Family: larger stop distance)
- Turn 9: added tcc_scale and speed factor, removed state machine? Actually changed to speed scaling based on TTC, but still many fails (4/7 passes). (Family: TTC scaling)
- Turn 10: reduced STOP_WAIT to 0.5, removed stop state, always detour. 7/9 passes, avg 66s, 2 collisions. (Family: aggressive detour, less stop)
- Turn 11 (current): added _danger_close detection with immediate evasion, but still 7/9 passes, avg ~80s, 2 fails (collision early, time limit). (Family: danger distance detection + existing stop/detour)

Thus families with most failures: family turn 9 (tcc_scale) and turn 10 (aggressive detour) have many fails. Turn 8 had best performance: 9/9 passes, avg 65s, no fails. But turn 8 didn't include danger detection; it just increased stop distance to 1.5. However, current code includes that plus danger detection, but still fails. Why? Possibly because danger detection triggers evasion, but evasion may cause more stop/detour episodes (leading to longer times). Also, collision still occurs because detection may be too late for fast approaching side/back objects.

Thus maybe the best direction is to revert to turn 8's settings (STOP_D=1.5) but also improve detection and evasion for side/back movers. The current code uses _danger_close (2m) but evasion may be insufficient; we can improve evasion by adjusting _evade to prioritize lateral moves or rotate in place when side/back mover is close.

Alternatively, we can incorporate a separate side/back detection and immediate rotation (detour) rather than using _evade which may try forward moves.

We need to propose a candidate direction: add a function _danger_side(pose, movers) that returns a rotation direction if any mover within DANGER_DIST is behind or side (bearing > 30°). Then in controller, if _danger_close and the mover is not front (maybe based on angle), we set state to "detour" and command rotation (0, +/-0.5) to turn away, then resume after safe.

Or we can modify _evade to consider the direction of movers and penalize forward motion when side/back mover present, increasing weight for rotation.

Another improvement: use robot body geometry for distance check: incorporate robot's rear length (-0.70) so that detection of rear objects uses that margin.

Also, to reduce overall time, we can increase speed scaling when safe: maybe increase v_nom scaling factor f (currently limited to max 1.0). Could increase max speed to 1.5 or 2.0 when gap large.

But we must keep within safe limits: _SAFE_GO = 0.6 is already used.

Potential new direction: combine larger stop distance (1.5) with side/back detection and immediate rotation, while also adjusting speed scaling to allow faster travel when safe.

Candidates: propose 3.

Candidate 1: Add side/back detection and immediate rotation (detour) when mover within DANGER_DIST but not front; new function _danger_side and modify controller to trigger detour state directly, bypassing _evade which may not handle side/back well. New_family: true (different from previous families). For: addresses collisions from side/back that current evasion misses. Risk: may cause unnecessary rotations, increasing time.

Candidate 2: Increase max speed scaling factor f to allow higher speeds when gap large, reducing overall travel time. Adjust f calculation to allow up to 1.5. New_family: true (speed scaling not previously used). For: reduces average sim time to meet budget. Risk: may increase collision risk if detection not timely.

Candidate 3: Adjust collision checking to account for robot rear (use body dimensions) in _danger_close and _is_safe, by expanding DANGER_DIST for rear region based on rear length. New_family: false? This is similar to earlier attempts of adjusting distances; but they haven't accounted for rear length. Could be new.

Select candidate 1 as primary: side/back detection and rotation.

Implementation steps:

- Define constant _DANGER_SIDE_ANGLE = math.radians(45) (or 30) for side/back detection.
- Add function _danger_side(pose, movers) that returns rotation direction (+1 or -1) if any mover within _DANGER_DIST and its bearing relative to robot > 30° (i.e., not in front cone). Use _to_robot to get coordinates, compute angle.
- In controller, after computing movers, call side_dir = _danger_side(pose, movers); if side_dir is not None: set c.state = "detour", c.detour_w = 0.5 * side_dir, c.detour_t = t; return 0.0, c.detour_w, False.
- Adjust _detour_side maybe to incorporate side detection.
- Ensure that when in detour state, the robot rotates in place until front gap becomes safe, then resume go.

Target: controller logic and new helper function.

Confidence: medium.
